name: Google Firestore
model: JSON-like documents in collections and subcollections; queries need indexes; real-time listeners push changes to web and mobile clients
engine_note: Multi-tenant service built on Google Spanner (per the ICDE 2023 paper); you never see the storage layer
consistency: Strongly consistent reads and queries. Multi-document transactions are serializable (pessimistic locks in Standard edition, optimistic in Enterprise; mobile and web SDKs always optimistic). Writes are synchronously replicated before acknowledgment.
scaling: Serverless: storage and traffic scale automatically inside a region or multi-region; you pay per read, write and stored GB. Ramp traffic gradually on new collections.
version_note: 2026-04-20: Firestore Enterprise edition in Native mode and Pipeline operations GA. Firestore with MongoDB compatibility went GA 2025-08-26. Latest note seen: 2026-09-04 (Security Rules simulator in console).
reach: Reach for it when a web or mobile app needs a serverless backend with live-updating data, offline sync and per-user security rules, without running servers.
avoid: Avoid when you need joins, ad hoc analytics, heavy aggregation, or predictable cost at very high read volumes (billed per document read).
escape: Clients need live-updating data and offline sync straight from the database, with no backend servers.
chat: Live message streams to web and mobile clients for a Firebase-built chat app; a natural fit there.
notes: Spanner as the backend is stated in the Firestore paper (ICDE 2023): 'Firestore's implementation leverages Google's infrastructure (in particular, Spanner)'. Firestore now has two editions (Standard, Enterprise) and a MongoDB-compatible API (GA 2025-08-26), which is a different API on the same service, not MongoDB software. Synchronous replication before acknowledgment is from the paper's strongly consistent design via Spanner; not re-checked in current docs. No Jepsen report.
